headline: Nahid Islam blames syndicates for price hikes of essentials
summary: The NCP Convener and Chief Whip of the National Parliament says dishonest syndicates are looting billions from the public through artificial price hikes.
details: Nahid Islam, Convener of the National Citizens Party (NCP) and Chief Whip of the National Parliament, has accused dishonest syndicates of driving up the prices of essential commodities.

In a Facebook post, he highlighted that Malta oranges are being sold at 550 BDT per kg, despite import documents showing a purchase price of 87 BDT. He calculated that the retail price should not exceed 250 BDT.

He alleged that syndicates have looted hundreds of crores of taka from the public over the last two months by artificially inflating Malta prices, despite a 22% increase in imports compared to last year.
Regarding Polao rice, he claimed it is being sold at 240 BDT when it should be 120 BDT, alleging that approximately 1,500 crore BDT has been looted in the last three months from this item alone.
Nahid Islam also noted that egg prices rose from 120 BDT to 160 BDT per dozen. He argued that while feed costs increased, the impact should have only raised the price by 1 BDT per egg, not 5 BDT.
He further pointed out that 12kg LPG cylinders are being sold at least 1,000 BDT above the government-fixed price, despite sufficient imports.
The NCP leader warned that the country is falling back into the grip of syndicates, similar to the previous fascist era, and demanded strict action against those involved.
caption:
From 87 BDT to 550 BDT per kg—Nahid Islam exposes how syndicates are looting billions from the public.

Nahid Islam, Convener of the National Citizens Party (NCP) and Chief Whip of the National Parliament, has accused dishonest syndicates of driving up the prices of essential commodities.

In a Facebook post, he highlighted that Malta oranges are being sold at 550 BDT per kg, despite import documents showing a purchase price of 87 BDT. He calculated that the retail price should not exceed 250 BDT.

He alleged that syndicates have looted hundreds of crores of taka from the public over the last two months by artificially inflating Malta prices, despite a 22% increase in imports compared to last year.

Regarding Polao rice, he claimed it is being sold at 240 BDT when it should be 120 BDT, alleging that approximately 1,500 crore BDT has been looted in the last three months from this item alone.

Nahid Islam also noted that egg prices rose from 120 BDT to 160 BDT per dozen. He argued that while feed costs increased, the impact should have only raised the price by 1 BDT per egg, not 5 BDT.

He further pointed out that 12kg LPG cylinders are being sold at least 1,000 BDT above the government-fixed price, despite sufficient imports.

The NCP leader warned that the country is falling back into the grip of syndicates, similar to the previous fascist era, and demanded strict action against those involved.

headline: 10,000 workers: Preparations to send workers to Malaysia at no cost underway
summary: The government is making arrangements to facilitate the migration of 10,000 Bangladeshi workers to Malaysia without any recruitment costs.
details: The government is preparing to send 10,000 Bangladeshi workers to Malaysia at no cost to the workers themselves.
This initiative aims to reduce the financial burden on migrant workers and eliminate the exploitative practices of middle-men in the recruitment process.
The move is part of a broader effort to ensure a fair and transparent migration system between the two countries.
Eligible candidates will be selected based on specific skill sets and requirements demanded by the Malaysian employers.
Further details regarding the application process, eligibility criteria, and timelines are expected to be announced soon by the relevant authorities.
caption:
